failure_class.name: workflow fusion loses a source capability

dependencies_on_this_tree.IMP-0177: receipt absent; fixture vectors stand in, disclosed
dependencies_on_this_tree.IMP-0182: receipt absent; fusion.splice-cite is the splice stand-in

implementation.rule: lost = union(capability_vector(source) for source in sources) - capability_vector(fusion); fire iff lost is nonempty
implementation.vector_derivation: Typed stage fields: capabilities, tools (tool:), gates (gate:), stop_rules (stop:), recovery (recovery:). Unreachable stages contribute nothing. A fusion's declared capability_vector cannot cover a dropped stage (overclaim control).

negative_controls.description: Drop unique-capability stage 'cite' from fusion.keep-all. Detector must fire and name cap.cite and gate:citation.required.
Drop scout-dup from fusion.redundant-scout. Tokens remain via scout; detector must stay silent.
After dropping cite, leave a declared capability_vector that still lists the lost tokens. Detector must still fire.

question_or_target: Assert that a fusion retains every capability of every source. The check is a computed set difference over capability vectors and it FIRES on a planted loss.

spec_anchor_note: Catalog row IMP-0191 names 'workflow fusion loses a source capability' as failure class (11333). A1 FAILURE-MODES.json maps that same name to FC-11332 / spec 11332, and maps 11333 to 'fused workflow performs worse than every source'. The detector keys on the named class string, records both integers, and does not silently retarget the worse-than-sources class.
